issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] Brace-leaf path normalization is not at parity with whole-token normalization. The operand judge now does inspect a brace token that was armed as a verb (this commit's fix), but when it expands the leaves it does not apply the `..`-collapsing that `normalize_path_token` applies to plain tokens. Measured parity table (literal vs. brace form, new hook): `.claude` ask/ask, `./.claude` ask/ask, `.//.claude` ask/ask, `.claude/` ask/ask, `./x/../.claude` ask/ask, `$PWD/.claude` ask/ask, `x/../.claude/settings.json` ask/ask — but `x/../.claude` ask/**allow**, `a/b/../../.claude` ask/**allow**, `.claude/../.claude` ask/**allow**. The leak is verb-independent (`{rm,-rf,…}`, `{find,…,-delete}`, `{mv,…,/tmp/s}`, `{rmdir,…}` all allow) and context-independent on the three non-substitution sites (bare, `bash -c`, adjacent assignment); `$( )`/backtick are BLOCKED by Layer 1/2, which is a gate, not a leak.

[security][critical][confidence:high] Isolated-lab confirmation of the above: in a fresh mktemp dir with a synthetic `.claude/settings.json` and an existing intermediate dir, `{rm,-rf,x/../.claude}`, `{rm,-rf,hooks/../.claude}`, `{rm,-rf,a/b/../../.claude}` and `{rm,-rf,.claude/../.claude}` each returned `allow` and each actually removed `.claude`. `hooks/../.claude` is a realistic in-repo spelling, so this is not a contrived shape.

[criteria][high][confidence:high] The generated suite cannot emit the leak above, by construction. `residual_key_for_context()` and the payload pool generate {construct} × {position} × {context} × {payload shape}, but the control-plane target inside each payload is drawn from a fixed two-element literal list. The 38th verdict's lesson was 'the axis was silently narrowed because payload content was never a factor'; the same narrowing now sits one level down, in the target-notation factor. Add target notation (`X/../<cp>`, `<cp>/../<cp>`, `a/b/../../<cp>`, `.//<cp>`, `$PWD/<cp>`, trailing-slash forms) as a generated factor rather than fixing this one instance.

[error][medium][confidence:high] New friction introduced by this commit (old → new differential). A comma brace with more than `__VERB_BRACE_BUDGET` (64) alternatives in any segment that also carries an arm-delete verb now asks even with no control-plane leaf anywhere: `cp x{f0,…,f119} /tmp/` was `allow` at 21889d0 and is `ask` at 1a0ba00; boundary measured at n=64 allow / n=65 ask. Same for `mv file{00,…,79}.txt /tmp/` and `rm -rf build/{d0,…,d79}`. Cause: the over-budget token returns undecided(2), the verb loop now declines to `continue` because the token contains a comma, and the operand judge then reports the benign token itself as the control-plane match (the ask reason literally names `x{f0,f1,…}`). The direction is fail-safe and it is ask (not deny), and SC-10(4) does declare 'over-cap → ask/armed', but this is a new false positive on commands with no control-plane leaf and it is neither tested nor attributed. The generated friction control (test 13) does not cover >64-alternative comma braces, which is why it passed.

[quality][medium][confidence:high] The 512-char cap fix is correct but was reached by trial: the in-file comment records that an earlier draft returned 1 for every non-comma token and broke the whole-token literal match, found only by self-probing. That the function's two exits (cap vs. literal comparison) can be swapped without any test failing indicates the cap boundary tests (generated test 10) pin only the ask side, not the match side.

acceptance: SC-11(1) fourth dimension — declared as a generated product, implemented with a fixed two-literal target pool; the dimension therefore does not cover the `{verb + control-plane operand}` value it claims to cover.
security: SC-11(5) in effect — the operand judge is now reached, but it under-normalizes brace leaves, so `{rm,-rf,x/../.claude}` / `{find,x/../.claude,-delete}` / `{mv,x/../.claude,/tmp/s}` / `{rmdir,x/../.claude}` reach allow and actually delete.

error_scenarios: New unattributed false positive at the >64-alternative comma-brace boundary for arm-delete verbs (`cp x{f0..f119} /tmp/`: allow at 21889d0, ask at 1a0ba00).

missing_criteria: The generation rule has no **operand-notation factor**. SC-11(1) generates construct × position × context × payload-shape; the control-plane target inside a payload is a fixed literal. Add a target-notation pool — at minimum `X/../<cp>`, `a/b/../../<cp>`, `<cp>/../<cp>`, `.//<cp>`, `./<cp>`, `<cp>/`, `<cp>//`, `$PWD/<cp>`, `~/<cp>` — and require every (payload shape × target notation) cell to be ask/BLOCKED or attributed.

No criterion requires **literal/expanded parity**: 'if `<verb> <operand>` is gated, then any construct that expands to the same words must be gated'. That single invariant would have caught both the 38th leak and this one, and it is checkable by generating the literal form alongside every generated cell and comparing decisions.

No friction criterion for caps: SC-10(4) says over-cap → ask/armed but nothing requires that over-cap over-gating be confined to segments that actually carry a control-plane-looking operand, nor that new over-gating be attributed. The `cp x{65 alternatives} /tmp/` regression is unowned as a result.
ambiguous_criteria: `ancestor_directory_operand`'s scope is now ambiguous enough that a real leak fell between it and SC-11. It is written about cwd-dependent ancestors (`.`, `..`, `*`), but a reader can also stretch it to cover `x/../.claude`. State explicitly that a path whose literal form is gated is never an ancestor-operand residual.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-11(2) accepts 'every generated cell is ask/BLOCKED or attributed' as the safety property, but a generation rule that under-generates satisfies it vacuously. The criterion needs a coverage obligation — e.g. each factor's pool must be enumerated from a named source (the guard's own normalization table for targets) rather than hand-listed in the test.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Next iteration: (a) normalize brace leaves through the same path pipeline as whole tokens (or, if that is too broad, treat any leaf containing `..` as undecided → armed), (b) add the operand-notation factor and the literal/expanded-parity check to the generated rule, (c) decide and record whether the >64-alternative over-gating is accepted friction or a bug, (d) keep SC-11(5) as written — it is correct.

recommended_fix: In `__control_plane_location_impl()`, run each expanded brace leaf through the same normalization that `normalize_path_token()` applies to a whole token (`..` collapsing in particular) before comparing against the control-plane set; failing that, return the undecided/armed value for any leaf containing a `..` segment. Then add target notation as a generated factor in tests/pre-bash-firewall-generated.bats and assert literal/expanded parity per cell.

items: SC-11(1) fourth dimension (expansion payload) — appropriate, add-only, and directly traceable to the 38th verdict's criteria_gaps. Not a scope inflation or a requirement relaxation.
SC-11(5) (consumed-as-verb ≠ exempt-from-operand-judge) — appropriate and correctly generalized, with a principled range-brace exception.
criteria_backfill_review.judgment: Both backfills are legitimate; neither widens scope nor weakens a requirement. Below the 3-item threshold that would trigger a spec/architecture re-review. The `ancestor_directory_operand` re-measurement is a correction of a prior round's mis-measurement, which is the behavior the calibration policy wants.
